summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Glucose/Galactose enter via apical SGLT1 (Na+ symport); Fructose via GLUT5; all exit via GLUT2. Fatty acids/monoglycerides diffuse from micelles into enterocyte, re-esterify into Triglycerides in SER, package into Chylomicrons in Golgi, and enter Lacteals.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
FAT ABSORPTION & LACTEAL PATHWAY
                       
   Intestinal Lumen: Triglycerides + Bile Salts ──► Emulsified Micelles (4–8 nm)
                                                             │
   Enterocyte Apical Membrane ◄── Passive Diffusion of Monoglycerides & Fatty Acids
               │
   Smooth ER (SER): Re-esterified into Triglycerides
               │
   Golgi Body: Encased in Apolipoproteins + Cholesterol ──► Chylomicrons (0.1–1.0 µm)
               │
   Basolateral Exocytosis ──► Enters Lacteals (Lymphatic Capillaries)
               │
   Thoracic Duct ──► Discharges into Left Subclavian Vein ──► Systemic Circulation
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 7.1 Carbohydrate & Protein Transporters
- **Glucose & Galactose**: Enter apical membrane via **SGLT1** (Sodium-Glucose Linked Transporter 1) via Secondary Active Transport coupled to $\text{Na}^+$ influx. Exit basolateral membrane into capillaries via **GLUT2** facilitated diffusion.
- **Fructose**: Absorbed via apical **GLUT5** facilitated diffusion. Exits via GLUT2.
- **Amino Acids**: Absorbed via $\text{Na}^+$-dependent secondary active transporters; small peptides enter via **PepT1** ($\text{H}^+$-peptide symporter).

### 7.2 Fat Absorption & Chylomicron Pathway
1. Luminal Micelles ($4\text{--}8\text{ nm}$) diffuse passively across enterocyte apical membrane.
2. **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)** re-esterifies fatty acids and monoglycerides into **Triglycerides**.
3. **Golgi Body** coats triglycerides with apolipoproteins and cholesterol to form **Chylomicrons ($0.1\text{--}1.0\ \mu\text{m}$)**.
4. Chylomicrons are exocytosed into **Lacteals (lymphatic capillaries)**, travelling via the **Thoracic Duct** to enter systemic venous blood at the left subclavian vein.
